mainTopic: The power of תשובה and תפילה to tear up a heavenly גזר דין for a יחיד and a ציבור, God's judgment on ראש השנה, and the months when messengers announce ראש חודש
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge from the previous daf: if תשובה can tear up a גזר דין, how can a verse say that after the sentence ה' no longer forgives? The גמרא answers that this applies only to a יחיד, and notes that even an individual's sentence is a מחלוקת תנאים: רבי מאיר says a תפילה שלימה can save him, רבי אלעזר says prayer helps only before the sentence, and רבי יצחק says crying out helps both before and after. Next the גמרא asks whether a ציבור's sentence can really be torn up, and answers that only a decree sealed with a שבועה is final, as with the oath against בית עלי. רבא and אביי teach that even בית עלי can find atonement through תורה, or through תורה with גמילות חסדים, and stories about רבה, אביי, and a family saved by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's advice illustrate this. רב teaches that a ציבור's decree can be torn up even after it is sealed, while a יחיד can reach ה' only at special times, the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. The גמרא then explains the משנה's phrase 'כבני מרון' in three ways, and רבי יוחנן adds that ה' sees everyone in one single glance. Finally a new משנה lists the months when בית דין's messengers go out to announce ראש חודש. The גמרא begins by asking why תמוז and טבת, which also have fasts, are not on the list, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Before the sentence versus after the sentence
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: one verse refers to the time before the גזר דין and the other to the time after it, which implies that repentance no longer helps once the sentence is issued.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (the verse is talking about) before the sentence; there (the verse is talking about) after the sentence!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a challenge it began on the previous daf. Two verses were reconciled by saying that one speaks of the time before a heavenly sentence and the other of the time after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses from the previous daf are 'ישא ה׳ פניו אליך' (God shows favor) and 'אשר לא ישא פנים' (He shows no favor). They were reconciled by saying the second describes the time after the גזר דין, when God no longer forgives. That suggests a final sentence cannot be undone by תשובה, which contradicts רבי יוחנן, who taught that תשובה tears up a person's גזר דין.

keyTerms.meaning: A final sentence or decree issued by the heavenly court
Here, meaning 'in this case' or 'in this verse'

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new teaching. It is the punchline of a challenge that started on the previous daf, and its exclamation mark signals 'so how can רבי יוחנן be right?'

phrases.english: Here — before the sentence is issued,
phrases.notes: The verse where God shows favor and forgives (ישא ה׳ פניו)

phrases.english: there — after the sentence is issued!
phrases.notes: The verse where God does not show favor (לא ישא פנים). This implies repentance no longer helps.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין, כָּאן לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge from the previous daf against רבי יוחנן's statement that תשובה tears up a sentence.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that תשובה tears up a person's גזר דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses are resolved by distinguishing before from after the sentence. That implies a post-sentence situation where repentance fails, which contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: This verse also refers to an individual
steps.stepSummary: The 'after the sentence, no help' verse speaks only about a יחיד. A ציבור can still be forgiven after its sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too (the verse speaks) about an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the verse about 'after the sentence' is talking about an individual person, not a whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא had already split cases into יחיד and ציבור. Here it uses the same split again ('here too'). Once an individual's sentence is issued, it stands. רבי יוחנן's statement still holds for a community, whose sentence can be torn up even afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, applying the same distinction as before
An individual person, as opposed to a community
A community, which has greater power to have a sentence annulled

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a central principle: the power of a community's prayer and repentance goes beyond that of an individual.

phrases.english: Here too, it refers to an individual.
phrases.notes: The 'after the sentence' verse is limited to a יחיד. A ציבור can still be forgiven.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the verse applies only to an individual
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the verse meant no one's sentence can be undone after it is issued.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an individual's sentence is fixed once issued. A community's sentence can still be torn up.

steps.title: An individual's sentence is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that whether an individual's sentence can be reversed is actually a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And (whether) an individual's sentence (can be reversed) is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It announces that the question of an individual's גזר דין is debated by תנאים, and it is about to bring a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 assumed that an individual's sentence cannot be undone. Now the גמרא points out that this is not agreed by everyone. Some תנאים hold that even an individual can be saved after his sentence.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים, the sages of the משנה era

phrases.english: And the sentence of an individual is a matter of dispute among Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַר דִּין דְּיָחִיד תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 2 by noting that the individual's case is itself debated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether an individual's issued sentence can be reversed is a מחלוקת תנאים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's case of two people in identical danger
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר describes two equally sick people, or two people facing the same court verdict. One recovers or is saved and the other is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught (in a ברייתא): רבי מאיר used to say: Two people went to bed (sick) with the same illness, and likewise two people went up to the tribunal to be judged with the same verdict. This one came down (from his bed) and that one did not come down; this one was saved and that one was not saved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the source for the dispute. רבי מאיר presents a puzzle: two people in exactly the same situation end up with different outcomes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that their illness and their verdict are 'the same' (שוה). Both, it seems, were already under the same heavenly sentence. So if one is saved, an individual's sentence can apparently be changed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Went up to bed, meaning they fell sick and were bedridden
A tribunal or place of judgment, especially for capital cases

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
Two people took to their beds, and their illness was the same,
and likewise two people went up to the tribunal to be judged
and their verdict was the same.
This one came down (recovered) and that one did not come down;
phrases.notes: Refers to the two sick people

phrases.english: this one was saved and that one was not saved.
phrases.notes: Refers to the two people on trial

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that proves the claim of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That an individual's sentence is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי מאיר about two people in identical danger

steps.title: Why did their outcomes differ?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר asks why two people in the same situation ended up so differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did this one come down and that one not come down; this one was saved and that one not saved?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי מאיר asks the obvious question: if everything was equal, what made the difference?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question focuses the reader on what each person did, since the external situations were identical. It prepares the answer that prayer made the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Came down, meaning recovered and got out of bed

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה יָרַד וְזֶה לֹא יָרַד,
phrases.english: For what reason did this one come down and that one not come down,
this one was saved and that one not saved?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה יָרַד וְזֶה לֹא יָרַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the case in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What caused the different outcomes for two people in identical situations?

steps.title: One prayed and was answered; the other was not
steps.stepSummary: Both prayed, but only one was answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one prayed and was answered, and that one prayed and was not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a first-level answer: the difference was whether their prayer was answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Note that both of them prayed. So simply praying does not explain the difference, and this pushes the question one level deeper.

phrases.english: This one prayed and was answered,
and that one prayed and was not answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הִתְפַּלֵּל וְנַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference was that one person's prayer was answered and the other's was not.

steps.title: Why was one prayer answered and not the other?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר digs deeper and asks why one prayer was answered and the other was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was this one answered and that one not answered?
steps.whatsHappening: Since both prayed, רבי מאיר asks what made one prayer succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This second question shows that the answer must lie in the quality of the prayer, not in whether a prayer was said at all.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה נַעֲנָה וְזֶה לֹא נַעֲנָה?
phrases.english: For what reason was this one answered and that one not answered?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה זֶה נַעֲנָה וְזֶה לֹא נַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did one prayer succeed and the other fail?

steps.title: A complete prayer is answered
steps.stepSummary: The one who prayed a תפילה שלימה, with a whole heart, was answered. The other was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one prayed a complete prayer and was answered; that one did not pray a complete prayer and was not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his final answer: what matters is praying a full, whole-hearted prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people faced the same sentence, yet one was saved through a תפילה שלימה. So רבי מאיר holds that an individual's sentence can be reversed even after it is issued. This is one side of the תנאים dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete prayer, said with full heart and concentration

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, an individual in the same situation as someone else can be saved by a תפילה שלימה. This means even an individual's sentence can be changed.

phrases.english: This one prayed a complete prayer, so he was answered,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה לֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה שְׁלֵימָה — לֹא נַעֲנָה
phrases.english: and that one did not pray a complete prayer, so he was not answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה שְׁלֵימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A whole-hearted prayer is answered, even for an individual under the same sentence as someone else.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the difference is timing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the different outcomes differently. One prayed before the sentence and the other after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Here (he prayed) before the sentence; there (he prayed) after the sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי מאיר's explanation. He says the deciding factor was when each person prayed, not how well he prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, a prayer said after an individual's גזר דין does not help. This is the opposing side of the תנאים dispute. The wording deliberately echoes the formula from step 1, now used as a ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: These words are identical to step 1, but they now serve a different purpose. There they were part of a challenge. Here they are רבי אלעזר's own explanation of רבי מאיר's case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Here, he prayed before the sentence was issued,
there, he prayed after the sentence was issued.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין, כָּאן לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing explanation to רבי מאיר's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual's prayer helps only before the גזר דין, not after.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: crying out always helps
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that crying out to ה' helps a person both before and after the sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Crying out is good for a person, both before the sentence and after the sentence.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a third view. Prayer and crying out to ה' are effective even after the sentence is issued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק directly rejects רבי אלעזר's timing limit. Like רבי מאיר, he holds that an individual's sentence can be changed. He stresses that it is never too late to cry out.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on an individual's sentence. רבי מאיר: a complete prayer can save. רבי אלעזר: prayer helps only before the sentence. רבי יצחק: crying out helps both before and after the sentence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the comforting idea that a person should never give up on prayer, even when a harsh decree seems already sealed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Crying out (to God) is good for a person
both before the sentence
and after the sentence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: יָפָה צְעָקָה לָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crying out to ה' is effective for an individual both before and after the גזר דין.

steps.title: Can a community's decree really be torn up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a decree against a צבור can be canceled. Two verses about ירושלים seem to show that repentance helps only before the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a community's decree really be torn up? One verse says, 'Wash your heart from evil,' which shows that washing helps. Another verse says, 'Even if you wash with lye and use much soap, your sin stays stained before Me,' which shows that washing does not help. Isn't the answer that the first verse is before the decree and the second is after it? If so, even a community cannot tear up a decree once it is made!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that a decree against a whole community can be torn up even after it is issued. It uses two verses about ירושלים, which is a community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse says repentance ("washing") works, and the other says it does not. The most natural way to fit them together is: before the decree it works, after the decree it does not. Since ירושלים is a צבור, this would mean that even a community's decree cannot be canceled once it is issued.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree or sentence from Heaven
A community, as opposed to a יחיד (individual)
Lye and soap, strong cleaning agents
Isn't it that? (introduces the suggested reading that creates the challenge)

phrases.english: And can the decree of a community be torn up?
But one verse says:
'Wash your heart from evil' (ירמיה 4:14)
And it is written: 'For even if you wash with lye'
'and use much soap'
'your sin is stained before Me' (ירמיה 2:22)

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: כָּאן קוֹדֶם גְּזַר דִּין,
phrases.english: Isn't it that here it is before the decree,
and here it is after the decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְזַר דִּין דְּצִבּוּר מִי מִיקְּרַע? וְהָא כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier idea that a community's decree can be canceled even after it is issued.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a decree against a צבור can be torn up after it is issued
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both verses address ירושלים, a community. The natural way to reconcile them splits before and after the decree, which implies that after the decree even a community's repentance does not help.

steps.title: Both verses are after the decree; the difference is an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both verses refer to the time after the decree. A decree sealed with a שבועה cannot be undone, while one without a שבועה can.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both verses are about the time after the decree, and there is no contradiction. One verse is about a decree that comes with an oath. The other is about a decree that comes without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the before/after reading of the two verses. It offers a different way to tell them apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer about timing. It is about the kind of decree. If ה' sealed the decree with a שבועה, repentance cannot cancel it ("your sin is stained"). If there is no oath, a community's repentance can cancel it even after the decree ("wash your heart"). This rescues the rule that a צבור can tear up a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both cases
And it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
An oath, here one sworn by ה' to keep the decree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer means a decree with an oath stops being a real decree. Both are full decrees. The oath only changes whether repentance can cancel it.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין,
phrases.english: No, both this and that are after the decree,
and it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה,
phrases.english: here it is a decree that has an oath with it,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה.
phrases.english: there it is a decree that has no oath with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): two different kinds of decrees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses differ by timing: before the decree versus after it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are after the decree. A decree with a שבועה cannot be torn up, and one without a שבועה can be torn up by a community.

steps.title: Source: a decree sealed by an oath cannot be torn up
steps.stepSummary: Following רב שמואל בר אמי (or רב שמואל בר נחמני) in the name of רבי יונתן, the גמרא proves from the oath against the house of עלי that a sworn decree cannot be canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב שמואל בר אמי. רב שמואל בר אמי said, and some say it was רב שמואל בר נחמני who said in the name of רבי יונתן: How do we know that a decree with an oath cannot be torn up? Because it says, 'Therefore I have sworn to the house of עלי that the sin of the house of עלי will not be atoned for with sacrifice or offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the idea in step 12, that an oath seals a decree so it cannot be canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in שמואל א shows ה' swearing that עלי's family's sin will not be atoned for. Because there is an oath, the decree stays in place. The גמרא also records two versions of who said this teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (an alternate version of who said it)

phrases.english: This is like רב שמואל בר אמי,
for רב שמואל בר אמי said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: and some say: רב שמואל בר נחמני said
in the name of רבי יונתן:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִגְזַר דִּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שְׁבוּעָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that a decree with an oath
cannot be torn up?
As it says: 'Therefore I have sworn to the house of עלי'
'that the sin of the house of עלי will not be atoned for'
'with sacrifice or with offering' (שמואל א 3:14)

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי. דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 12 with a verse.
steps.raayaObject: A decree sealed with a שבועה cannot be torn up
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 3:14, the oath to the house of עלי
steps.whyThisMatters: This verse becomes the base for the next teachings about how עלי's family can still find atonement.

steps.title: רבא: atonement through Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the verse narrowly. Sacrifices cannot atone for the house of עלי, but תורה can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for, but it is atoned for with תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a precise reading of the verse about עלי. He finds a way out of the oath's full harshness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath names only sacrifices and offerings. So רבא concludes that other paths, namely learning תורה, can still bring atonement. The oath holds, but only for what it explicitly says.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for with Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּזֶבַח וּבַמִּנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the verse quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath blocks atonement only through sacrifices. תורה still atones for the house of עלי.
steps.confusionAlert: The story that follows names רבה, not רבא. Many texts read רבה in this statement too, which would match the story. Here we follow the text exactly as given.

steps.title: אביי: atonement through Torah and kindness
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that both תורה and גמילות חסדים atone for the house of עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for, but it is atoned for with תורה and with גמילות חסדים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second view on the same verse. He widens the ways atonement can come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי agrees that sacrifices are blocked. But he holds that atonement comes through תורה together with גמילות חסדים, not through תורה alone.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With sacrifice and offering it is not atoned for,
but it is atoned for with Torah and acts of kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּזֶבַח וּמִנְחָה אֵינוֹ מִתְכַּפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, fuller view than the one in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה together with גמילות חסדים atones for the house of עלי.

steps.title: רבה and אביי's lifespans
steps.stepSummary: רבה and אביי both came from בית עלי. רבה, who mainly learned תורה, lived 40 years. אביי, who learned תורה and also did גמילות חסדים, lived 60 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and אביי came from בית עלי. רבה, who was busy with תורה, lived forty years. אביי, who was busy with תורה and גמילות חסדים, lived sixty years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that shows the two views from steps 14 and 15 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family of עלי was cursed to die young. Both men lived longer than that curse would suggest, so תורה helped. But אביי, who added kindness, lived even longer. This shows the extra power of גמילות חסדים, matching אביי's view.
steps.whatToRemember: A decree sealed with a שבועה cannot be torn up through repentance. Even so, the oath on בית עלי blocks only sacrifices. תורה, and even more so תורה with גמילות חסדים, can still bring atonement and long life.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Abaye came from the house of Eli.
Rabbah, who was busy with Torah,
lived forty years;
Abaye, who was busy with Torah and acts of kindness,
lived sixty years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְאַבָּיֵי מִדְּבֵית עֵלִי קָאָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the views in steps 14 and 15.
steps.raayaObject: תורה atones for בית עלי, and תורה with גמילות חסדים atones even more
steps.raayaSupportSource: The lifespans of רבה (40 years) and אביי (60 years)

steps.title: A family descended from עלי is saved by learning תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a family in ירושלים whose members died at eighteen. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי suggested they came from the house of עלי and told them to learn תורה. They learned and they lived.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a family in ירושלים whose members kept dying at age eighteen. They came and told רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He said to them: Maybe you come from the family of עלי, about whom it is written, 'All the increase of your house will die as young men.' Go learn תורה and you will live. They went, learned תורה, and lived. People then called the family by רבן יוחנן's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story from a ברייתא. It shows that learning תורה can cancel the curse on the house of עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said that sacrifices cannot atone for בית עלי, but תורה can. This story is a real case of exactly that. The family's only remedy was עסק התורה, and it worked.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this introduces a ברייתא)
The family of עלי the כהן גדול, who were cursed to die young
The increase of your house, meaning your descendants

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that the sworn decree against בית עלי is closed to sacrifices but still open to תורה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was one family in Jerusalem
whose dead used to die
at eighteen years old.

phrases.aramaic: בָּאוּ וְהוֹדִיעוּ אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: They came and told Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
he said to them:
Perhaps you are from the family of Eli,
about whom it is written:
'And all the increase of your house shall die as young men' —
go and engage in Torah and live.
They went and engaged in Torah and lived.
And people would call it
'the family of Rabban Yochanan,' after his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִשְׁפָּחָה אַחַת הָיְתָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another real-life support, after רבה and אביי, that תורה atones for בית עלי.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that תורה can atone for the house of עלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a family saved by learning תורה at the advice of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.whatToRemember: The decree on בית עלי cannot be fixed with קרבנות, but תורה (and גמילות חסדים) can soften it.

steps.title: A decree against the community is not sealed
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר איניא, in the name of רב, asks for the source that a גזר דין against a צבור is never sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר איניא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a decree against a community is not sealed?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: a decree against a whole community is not sealed. It is phrased as 'from where do we know,' so a verse is expected next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps showed that a decree on a single family, sealed with a שבועה, stays in place. Now the גמרא turns to the צבור and says its decree is different and more flexible.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Inya said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that the decree of a community
is not sealed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the decree on one family (בית עלי) to decrees on a whole community.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A decree against a צבור is not sealed.

steps.title: A verse says the community's sin is 'sealed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a verse in ירמיהו says 'נכתם עונך לפני,' which suggests the community's sentence is sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not sealed?! But it is written: 'Your sin is sealed before Me'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's wording. A verse speaks to the nation and says its sin is 'נכתם,' sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו is speaking to the whole people, so this is a צבור. If the verse calls their sin sealed, then it is not correct to say a צבור's decree is never sealed.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (introduces a verse that contradicts)
Your sin is stained or sealed (read here like נחתם)

steps.confusionAlert: נכתם (with a כ) literally means 'stained.' The גמרא reads it like נחתם, 'sealed,' because the two words sound alike.

phrases.english: It is not sealed?!
But it is written: 'Your iniquity is sealed before Me'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ נֶחְתָּם?! וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב's statement in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a צבור's decree is never sealed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse addressed to the nation calls its sin 'sealed,' so a צבור's decree can be sealed.

steps.title: Even when sealed, the community's decree can be torn up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rephrases רב's teaching: a צבור's decree can be sealed, but it can still be torn up. The source is 'כה׳ אלהינו בכל קראנו אליו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: even though it is sealed, it is torn up, as it says: 'Like ה׳ our God whenever we call to Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. A community's decree can be sealed, but it can still be ripped up through prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse from ירמיהו is accepted: the decree can be sealed. The new point is that sealing does not make it final for a צבור. The verse says God answers the nation 'whenever we call,' at any time.

phrases.english: Rather:
even though it is sealed, it is torn up,
as it is said:
'As ה׳ our God is, whenever we call to Him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַף עַל גַּב שֶׁנֶּחְתָּם — נִקְרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by rewording רב's statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A צבור's decree is never sealed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A צבור's decree can be sealed, but it can still be torn up whenever they call out to God.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the special power of communal prayer to change even a sealed decree.

steps.title: A verse says to seek God only when He can be found
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges with 'דרשו ה׳ בהמצאו,' which suggests there are only certain times when God can be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'Seek ה׳ when He can be found'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another verse against the idea that God answers at any time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When He can be found' implies that at other times He cannot be found. That clashes with 'בכל קראנו אליו,' which means God answers whenever we call.

keyTerms.meaning: Seek ה׳ while He may be found

phrases.english: But it is written: 'Seek ה׳ when He can be found'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: דִּרְשׁוּ ה׳ בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse used in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'בכל קראנו אליו' as meaning God answers at all times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישעיהו implies there are limited times when God can be found.

steps.title: One verse is about an individual, the other about a community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: 'דרשו ה׳ בהמצאו' speaks of a יחיד, and 'בכל קראנו' speaks of a צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is talking about an individual; here it is talking about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by giving each verse a different subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יחיד has only special times when God is close. A צבור can reach God at any time. Both verses are true, each in its own case.

phrases.english: There, it is about an individual;
here, it is about a community.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּיָחִיד, הָכָא בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses speak about the same people, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: A יחיד is answered only at special times. A צבור is answered at any time.
steps.whatToRemember: A צבור can tear up even a sealed decree at any time. A יחיד has only limited windows.

steps.title: When is God close to an individual?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: when exactly is the time when a יחיד can 'find' God?
steps.simpleTranslation: For an individual, when is it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next step. If a יחיד has only special times, which times are they?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said a יחיד can find God only 'בהמצאו,' when He can be found. Now the גמרא wants that time defined.

phrases.english: For an individual, when is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיָחִיד, אֵימַת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the יחיד case from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific time when God is 'found' by a יחיד

steps.title: The ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה answers that the time is the עשרה ימים between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה said: These are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה gives the answer. The special window for a יחיד is the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains 'בהמצאו' with a set time on the calendar. During these days even a single person's prayer and תשובה can change his decree.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, the day of judgment

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh said:
These are the ten days
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אֵלּוּ עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עשרה ימים between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the special power of עשרת ימי תשובה.

steps.title: Why did נבל die only after ten days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a verse saying God struck נבל 'about ten days' later and asks what those ten days were for.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it was about ten days, and ה׳ struck נבל.' What were these ten days for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a verse in which נבל's punishment was delayed ten days. This sets up two answers, one of which ties back to the עשרה ימים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבל had already earned death for insulting דוד, so why wait ten days? The question opens the way to connect the delay with the עשרה ימים just mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: The rich man who insulted דוד's servants (שמואל א כה)
What is their function? What are they doing here?

phrases.english: 'And it was about ten days later,
and ה׳ struck Naval' —
what is the purpose of these ten days?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים מַאי עֲבִידְתַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a verse about ten days, which may connect to the עשרה ימים of step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the ten-day delay before נבל's death

steps.title: The ten days match ten meals נבל gave
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the ten days match the ten לגימות, portions of food, that נבל gave to דוד's servants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They correspond to the ten mouthfuls that נבל gave to דוד's servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: נבל got one day of delay for each of the ten portions of food he gave דוד's servants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer the delay is a reward for a small good deed. It has nothing to do with ראש השנה. God does not hold back reward even from a wicked person.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Corresponding to the ten mouthfuls
that Naval gave to David's servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר לְגִימוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to step 25's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days were a reward for the ten portions of food נבל gave דוד's servants.

steps.title: The ten days were the days of repentance
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the ten days were the עשרה ימים between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, a last chance for נבל to do תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: These are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: נבל was given the עשרה ימים בין ראש השנה ליום הכפורים as a final window to repent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the delay matches the window of תשובה that רבה בר אבוה taught in step 24. The same authority (רבה בר אבוה) now shows the idea at work in a verse: נבל's punishment waited through the ten days of repentance, and only afterward was he struck.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on רבה בר אבוה's teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The text here is repeated word for word from step 24, but it now does something different. Here it explains the ten-day delay in נבל's story.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
These are the ten days
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer, in place of רב's, and links back to step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days were the עשרת ימי תשובה, a final chance for נבל to repent.
steps.whatToRemember: For a יחיד, the special time when God is close is the עשרה ימים between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. Even נבל was given this window before his punishment.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: everyone passes before God כבני מרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that on ראש השנה all people pass before God 'כבני מרון,' so that it can explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה, all who come into the world pass before Him 'כבני מרון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes a line from the משנה. This is a setup line: the next step will ask what the unusual phrase 'כבני מרון' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that on ראש השנה every human being is judged by God. The hard words are 'כבני מרון,' which describe how people pass before Him. The גמרא brings up the line only so it can explain those words.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who come into the world, meaning all human beings
Pass before Him, meaning they are judged by God
An unclear phrase describing how people pass before God; the next steps explain it

phrases.english: On Rosh HaShana
all who come into the world
pass before Him like benei maron.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה earlier in the perek

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as the setup of the question)
steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כׇּל בָּאֵי הָעוֹלָם עוֹבְרִין לְפָנָיו כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of the ten days of תשובה back to explaining a phrase in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה all people are judged by God, passing before Him 'כבני מרון.'

steps.title: What does כבני מרון mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase 'כבני מרון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'כבני מרון'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what does 'כבני מרון' mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the משנה. It is a request to define words. Three different answers follow.

phrases.english: What is 'like benei maron'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the phrase just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the words 'כבני מרון'

steps.title: Babylonian explanation: like a flock of sheep
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they explained 'כבני מרון' as 'כבני אמרנא,' like sheep passing one by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here in בבל they translated it: like a flock of sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the sages in בבל said it means like sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shepherd counts his sheep as they pass through a narrow opening one at a time. In the same way, every person passes before God one by one to be judged.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in בבל) they explained or translated it

phrases.english: Here they translated it: like a flock of sheep.
phrases.notes: 'מרון' is read as related to the Aramaic 'אמרנא,' sheep

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא תַּרְגִּימוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like sheep that pass one by one to be counted

steps.title: ריש לקיש: like the steep ascent of בית מרון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains it as the narrow, steep path up to בית מרון, where people climb one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: like the ascent of בית מרון.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation: ריש לקיש says it refers to the steep climbing path of בית מרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The path was so narrow that people had to go up in single file. Someone standing at the top could see every climber. The picture is again each person passing before God individually.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
The steep ascent (climbing path) of the place called בית מרון

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Like the ascent of Beit Maron.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר כְּמַעֲלוֹת בֵּית מָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different explanation of the same phrase
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like climbers going single file up the narrow path of בית מרון

steps.title: שמואל: like the soldiers of בית דוד
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains it as the soldiers of the army of בית דוד, reviewed in formation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: like the soldiers of בית דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation: like the soldiers of דוד המלך's army.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An army is inspected as it marches past, and the commander takes in all the soldiers at once. This picture adds a new idea: God reviews everyone together, which sets up רבי יוחנן's statement in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The royal house of King David

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Like the soldiers of the house of David.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כַּחֲיָילוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the same phrase
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like soldiers of דוד's army reviewed by their commander

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: everyone is reviewed in one single look
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: even though people pass one by one, God sees them all in one single glance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: and they are all scanned in a single scan.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds an important point: God looks at all people in one single look.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pictures of passing one by one might suggest that judgment takes a long time, one person after another. רבי יוחנן says no. God sees everyone at the same moment, and each person is still judged individually.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main idea the rest of this section works to prove from a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And they are all scanned in a single scan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן נִסְקָרִין בִּסְקִירָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that, despite the 'one-by-one' images, God sees all at once
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All people are judged by God in one single glance.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a verse as support
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says we can learn רבי יוחנן's idea from the פסוק 'היוצר יחד לבם המבין אל כל מעשיהם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: we too learned this: 'He who fashions their hearts together, who understands all their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'we too learned this': the פסוק from תהלים quoted in our own משנה supports רבי יוחנן. The next steps will check how the פסוק should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יחד' (together) in the פסוק is the key. רב נחמן בר יצחק will argue that it means God sees all hearts together, in one look.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (a source that supports the statement)
The One who forms, the Creator

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We too have learned it:
"He who fashions their hearts together,
who understands all their deeds."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone is judged in one look
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים לג:טו, 'היוצר יחד לבם המבין אל כל מעשיהם'

steps.title: What is the verse saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק actually means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask how to read the פסוק. This sets up a test of two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if 'יחד' refers to God seeing everyone at once. The גמרא first has to rule out the other possible meaning.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the meaning of the פסוק just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct meaning of 'יחד' in the פסוק

steps.title: Rejecting the reading that God made all hearts alike
steps.stepSummary: One could read the פסוק as saying God made all people's hearts the same. But we see that this is not true, so that reading is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that He created everyone and makes their hearts united with one another, but we see that this is not so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reading, that God made everyone's hearts alike, and rejects it because real life shows otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People clearly think and feel differently, so the פסוק cannot mean that all hearts are the same. Ruling this out leaves only the other reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading that will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is NOT the גמרא's conclusion. It is a reading that is brought up only to be rejected.

phrases.english: If you say this is what it is saying:
that He created everyone
and unites their hearts with one another,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּלָאו הָכִי הוּא!
phrases.english: but we see that it is not so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible reading of the פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading that 'יחד' means all hearts are made alike
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts what we see: people's hearts are not alike

steps.title: Correct reading: God sees all hearts together
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק must mean that the Creator sees all hearts together and understands all their deeds. This proves רבי יוחנן's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it is saying: The Creator sees their hearts together and understands all their deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading: 'יחד' describes how God sees, all at once. That completes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 'hearts are alike' reading is ruled out, 'יחד' must describe God's seeing. God sees all hearts together, in one look, exactly as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that (introduces the accepted reading)

steps.whatToRemember: On ראש השנה each person is judged individually ('כבני מרון'), yet God sees everyone in one single look, as the פסוק 'היוצר יחד לבם' shows.

phrases.english: Rather, is this not what it is saying:
The Creator sees their hearts together
and understands all their deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining reading after step 36's rejection, completing the proof
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'יחד' means God sees all hearts together at once, which supports רבי יוחנן

steps.title: New משנה: the six months when messengers go out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists six months in which the שלוחים of בית דין go out to announce when ראש חודש was set, and the holiday that makes each one necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In six months the messengers go out: in ניסן because of פסח, in אב because of the fast, in אלול because of ראש השנה, in תשרי to set the festivals correctly, in כסלו because of חנוכה, and in אדר because of פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the months in which בית דין sent messengers to tell distant communities which day was ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communities far away could not know whether the month began on day 30 or 31, so they could not know which day was the holiday. Messengers went out only in months that have a holiday whose date depends on ראש חודש. In תשרי this is for יום כפור and סוכות, and in אלול it is so people can work out when ראש השנה will fall.

keyTerms.meaning: Abbreviation of מתניתין: 'our משנה,' marking the start of a new משנה
Fast; here, the fast of תשעה באב
Setting the festivals correctly (יום כפור and סוכות)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ עַל שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים הַשְּׁלוּחִין יוֹצְאִין:
phrases.english: MISHNA: In six months the messengers go out:
in Nisan, because of Pesach;
in Av, because of the fast;
in Elul, because of Rosh HaShana;
in Tishrei, to set the festivals correctly;
in Kislev, because of Chanukah;
and in Adar, because of Purim.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים הַשְּׁלוּחִין יוֹצְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין sends messengers in ניסן, אב, אלול, תשרי, כסלו, and אדר, the months whose holidays depend on knowing the date of ראש חודש.

steps.title: In the time of the בית המקדש, messengers also went out in אייר
steps.stepSummary: When the בית המקדש stood, messengers also went out in אייר because of פסח קטן (פסח שני).
steps.simpleTranslation: And when the בית המקדש was standing, they would also go out in אייר because of 'פסח קטן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a seventh month that applied only while the בית המקדש stood: אייר, because of פסח שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who could not bring the קרבן פסח in ניסן brought it on the 14th of אייר. That date mattered only when קרבנות were offered, so after the חורבן there was no need to send messengers in אייר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Small Pesach,' meaning פסח שני on 14 אייר

steps.confusionAlert: 'פסח קטן' is not a minor part of regular פסח. It is פסח שני, the second chance to bring the קרבן פסח, one month later.
steps.whatToRemember: Messengers went out in six months, and in seven while the בית המקדש stood, to announce the date of ראש חודש for holidays that depend on it.

phrases.english: And when the Temple was standing,
they would also go out in Iyar
because of the small Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהָיָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים יוֹצְאִין אַף עַל אִיָּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a month that applied only in the time of the בית המקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the בית המקדש stood, messengers also went out in אייר for פסח שני.

steps.title: Why not also send messengers for תמוז and טבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list. If messengers go out in אב because of the fast, they should also go out in תמוז and טבת, which have fasts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let the messengers also go out for תמוז and טבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a challenge. It asks why the משנה's list of months leaves out תמוז and טבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts אב because people need the right date to keep the fast of תשעה באב. But שבעה עשר בתמוז and עשרה בטבת are also public fasts. So by the משנה's own logic, those months should be on the list too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
And let them go out (the messengers)
The month of Tammuz, which has the fast of the 17th (שבעה עשר בתמוז)
The month of Tevet, which has the fast of the 10th (עשרה בטבת)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never says the word 'fast' here. You have to bring in the reason from the משנה yourself: messengers go out in אב because of the fast. That is why תמוז and טבת seem to belong on the list.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: And let them also go out for Tammuz and Tevet!
phrases.notes: Implied reasoning: those months also have public fast days, like Av.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְּקוּ נָמֵי אַתַּמּוּז וְטֵבֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list of months in the משנה (Step 38) by applying its own reason for אב to other fast months.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of six months for sending messengers, especially the inclusion of אב because of its fast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a public fast is enough reason to send messengers in אב, then תמוז and טבת, which also have public fasts, should get messengers as well. Leaving them out seems inconsistent.
